text:
Alex: Heads up — I'm scheduling a tf apply for IAM role consolidation during the release window at 02:00 UTC. This will touch tenant bindings in modules/tenants/* and the cross-account trust.
Maria: Thanks. Which provider aliases are changing? any shuffling of k8s service accounts? :thinking_face:
Alex: No k8s SA changes. Provider alias changes for aws.main and aws.security (we're switching a couple of accounts to assume_role). Plan shows 32 resources to change, 6 to recreate. I pushed the plan to the PR.
Oliver: Can you paste the risky bits? I can join the quick preflight call at 01:30 UTC.
Alex: Sure — snippet from plan: 
```
- aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.old -> aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.new (recreate)
+ module.tenants["acme"].aws_iam_role.tenant_role (update)
```
Maria: If any attachment recreates we might temporarily drop allowed assume principals. Need a pinned fallback role.
Samira: We should pin the infra provider version for this apply so deploybot uses the expected provider binary. Suggest pinning terraform-provider-aws v4.60.0 in the release branch.
Alex: Good call. I'll add a provider pin and a preflight remote state snapshot step in the runbook.
DeployBot: [scheduled] tf-apply queued for 2025-06-12 02:00:00 UTC on branch release/2025-06. Trigger: alex. ID: db-1752468901.
infra-oncall: Quick reminder — maintainers on call: @Samira @Oliver. If latency spikes or errors we roll back to the last known-good commit and re-run apply with the escape hatch flag.
Maria: Rollback decision criteria proposal: immediate rollback if >5% auth failures for tenant API in 5m after cutover OR any high-severity (500) errors in control-plane auth logs. Otherwise, hold and patch.
Samira: Agree. Add an automated smoke test post-apply: token exchange + list-roles for 10 sample tenants. If smoke fails, deploybot abort and run rollback.
Alex: I'll add smoke steps. Also adding a 15m traffic shadow period where new binding is applied but traffic still routed to old role for critical paths.
Oliver: How do we do the shadow? traffic-routing config or use canary policy in the auth service?
Alex: Canary in auth service — config flag in configmap that maps 10% of traffic to new role for 15m, then 100% if healthy. We can flip via /ops/feature-toggle.
Maria: Confirming read-only escalation path: if rollback needed, we run `git revert <commit>` on infra branch, re-run deploybot with --force-revert, and notify security for any orphaned assume-roles.
Samira: I'll prepare the revert PR template and a checklist: snapshot remote state, export bindings, run smoke, watch metrics.
DeployBot: [preflight] Running plan sanity checks now. Provider pin detected: terraform-provider-aws v4.60.0. Plan hash: sha256:abcd...
Alex: Thanks. If preflight passes I'll merge the branch at 01:45 and put the apply on manual hold until 02:00. Please be near Slack + pager.
Maria: I'll be on the preflight call and ready to kick rollback if smoke fails.
Samira: Oncall will monitor cloudwatch alarms and the auth service SLO dashboard.
Oliver: Copy. If anything weird appears, @infra-oncall escalate to oncall-ops.
DeployBot: [status] Preflight passed. No drift detected. Apply window: 02:00 — proceeding to queued state.
Alex: Merging now. Everyone — thumbs if you can be available at 01:55 UTC.
Maria: 👍
Samira: 👍
Oliver: 👍
infra-oncall: I'll be watching.
Alex: Final note — escape hatch command: `./scripts/infra-revert.sh --apply --branch release/2025-06 --force-revert` (keeps state snapshot). Don't run unless we confirm rollback criteria.
Maria: Saved. See you on the call. :white_check_mark:
